en.title: The Witcher 3 Path Tracing Demands an RTX 5080 for Ultimate Visuals
en.summary: CD Projekt Red has unveiled the daunting system requirements for The Witcher 3's path tracing update, revealing that achieving the highest fidelity will require bleeding-edge hardware. While basic gameplay remains accessible, the path to photorealism is a significant leap in graphical demand.
en.body:
The winds of Kaer Morhen may be blowing, but they’re also demanding a powerful gust of GPU power. CD Projekt Red has officially detailed the system requirements for the highly anticipated path tracing update to **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt**, and for those dreaming of Geralt’s world rendered with unparalleled realism, the price of admission is steep. While the base game’s update aims for accessibility, the ultimate visual experience, particularly with path tracing enabled, requires hardware that is currently at the very forefront of PC gaming technology.

For players looking to experience **The Witcher 3** on its lowest settings at a stable 30 frames per second, the hardware demands are surprisingly modest. A configuration featuring an **Nvidia GeForce GTX 1660**, an **AMD Radeon RX 550 XT**, or an **Intel Arc A580**, coupled with an **Intel Core i5 8400** or **AMD Ryzen 5 2600**, will suffice. This ensures that a broad spectrum of players can still jump back into the Continent with improved visuals. However, the true graphical feast – the path tracing preset – paints a very different picture. To achieve this, gamers will need to equip themselves with a top-tier CPU like an **Intel Core i9 13900K** or an **AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D**, and crucially, an **Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080** graphics card.

## The Path to Photorealism Demands the Best

This significant jump in requirements is, of course, due to the intensive nature of path tracing. This advanced rendering technique simulates the physical behavior of light in real-time, offering more accurate shadows, reflections, and global illumination, making the game world feel more lifelike than ever before. To reach an estimated 60 frames per second at 4K resolution with path tracing, players will not only need the aforementioned high-end components but will also rely heavily on upscaling technologies like DLSS and frame generation. CD Projekt Red has not specified the exact DLSS preset or frame generation method required, but it’s clear that these AI-driven features are essential for making such demanding settings playable. This also suggests that performance will be more manageable at lower resolutions like 1440p or 1080p, even with path tracing enabled.

## Community Reaction and Performance Expectations

The reveal of these requirements has predictably sparked discussions within the **Witcher** community. Many fans are excited about the prospect of experiencing **The Witcher 3** with such cutting-edge graphical fidelity, seeing it as the ultimate way to revisit a beloved world. However, the astronomical GPU requirement for the highest settings has also led to a dose of reality for many. The RTX 5080 is currently among the most powerful, and most expensive, GPUs available, meaning that truly experiencing **The Witcher 3** with full path tracing will be a luxury for only the most dedicated and well-equipped enthusiasts. While the game offers a range of graphical options, the stark contrast between the minimum and ultra-path tracing requirements highlights the ever-increasing demands of modern game development and the reliance on powerful hardware to push graphical boundaries.

## What's Next

With the path tracing update now live, players can explore the enhanced visuals of **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt** based on their hardware capabilities. Further details on specific DLSS and frame generation settings may emerge as players dive deeper into the game and share their experiences, allowing for more precise performance tuning.

content_raw: We all know that path tracing is a bit of a GPU hog, and if you plan on running it in the remaster of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , you're going to need a beefy and relatively new rig for this graphical mode. However, to get the game up and running on the lowest settings at 30 fps, you won't need a very recent GPU. With The Witcher 3 Remastered going live today, CD Projekt Red has shared what you can expect to run with every major CPU and GPU brand, with Low graphics at 30 fps requiring a relatively meagre Nvidia GeForce GTX 1660 / AMD Radeon RX 550 XT / Intel Arc A580 , plus an Intel Core i5 8400 or AMD Ryzen 5 2600. However, for path tracing, you will need an Intel Core i9 13900K or AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D , paired with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 . To get the estimated 60 fps at 4K, you will have to not only run DLSS, but you will need to use frame generation. That does mean it should fare better at 1440p or 1080p. CD Projekt Red does not specify which level of upscaling or type of frame generation is present for this setting, though. As we saw in our investigation of Pragmata's path tracing earlier this year, we are expecting The Witcher 3 Remastered's path tracing to offer better shadows and highlights to generally make the world feel more 'real'. However, whether or not it's worth the hit to performance will be dependent on your tastes (and your rig). I'm not personally sold on even ray tracing's benefits all of the time, so it would be a tough sell for me, even if I had a rig good enough to run it.
